issues.title: Remaining criteria count displays %d instead of a number on Minecraft 26.2
issues.body: On Minecraft 26.2, Better Advancements shows "%d remaining" instead of the actual number. For example, Adventuring Time shows 52/55 completed, but the tooltip says "%d remaining" instead of "3 remaining". I fixed this locally by changing "%d" to "%s" in the translation. It would be great to have this fixed in an official update when you have a chance. For my own version, I also made it show missing requirement names by default, with completed requirements first and missing ones at the end. If you could add something like that, it would be nice too! Thanks for the mod! Before: After fixing the remaining count: My version with the additional features: Here’s the small fix I used in `assets/betteradvancements/lang/en_us.json`: ```diff - "betteradvancements.remaining": "%d remaining", + "betteradvancements.remaining": "%s remaining", ``` The other language files need the same `%d` to `%s` change, keeping their translated text. For my own version, I also made these small changes. If you could include something similar, it would be nice! In `CriteriaDetail.java`, show completed and missing requirements by default: ```diff - DEFAULT("Default", "List which criteria you have already obtained", true, false), + DEFAULT("Default", "Show both obtained and unobtained criteria", true, true), ``` In `CriterionGrid.java`, collect missing requirements separately: ```diff List cellContents = new ArrayList<>(); + List missingContents = new ArrayList<>(); ``` Inside the unfinished-criterion branch, add the missing requirement to that separate list: ```diff - cellContents.add(text); + missingContents.add(text); ``` Then, immediately after the criteria loop, append the missing requirements so they appear after the completed ones: ```java cellContents.addAll(missingContents); ```

issues.title: Modrinth: the 1.20.1 NeoForge jar of 0.6.0.73 is tagged as loader "forge" (and sorts first in the API)
issues.body:
Not a code bug — a Modrinth metadata one, but it silently hands the wrong jar to anything that fetches automatically.

### What I see

`GET /v2/project/better-advancements/version?game_versions=["1.20.1"]` returns, in this order:

| version | `loaders` | primary file |
| - | - | - |
| 0.6.0.73 | `["forge"]` | `BetterAdvancements-NeoForge-1.20.1-0.6.0.73.jar` |
| 0.6.0.73 | `["fabric"]` | `BetterAdvancements-Fabric-1.20.1-0.6.0.73.jar` |
| 0.6.0.73 | `["forge"]` | `BetterAdvancements-Forge-1.20.1-0.6.0.73.jar` |

So the **NeoForge** file is tagged `forge`, and there are two entries claiming `forge` for the same version. The older 0.4.2.59 / 0.4.2.60 entries look right (`neoforge` for the NeoForge file), and 0.4.2.25 has the same mix-up as 0.6.0.73.

### Why it bites

Filtering by `loaders=["forge"]` and taking the first result — which is the obvious way to write a fetcher — yields the **NeoForge** jar for a Forge 1.20.1 instance. The correct Forge file is third in the list, so nothing about the response signals that the first one is wrong.

I hit this on a Forge 1.20.1 pack and now skip any candidate whose filename declares a different loader, but that is a workaround on my side.

### Suggested fix

Re-tag the 0.6.0.73 (and 0.4.2.25) NeoForge files as `neoforge` on Modrinth. No jar changes needed.

issues.title: Servers are marked incompatible when installed client-side only.
issues.body:
It's my understanding that this mod is client-side only. (I could be wrong?)

It's also my understanding that you should be able to connect to servers that do not have this mod installed, if you have the mod installed on your client.

In fact, I have a server with (many) mods installed, but this mod is not installed on the server, and my client can connect to my server with this mod installed on my client. 

So far? So good.

*However*, the server, in the server listing menu, reports to the client that the client is incompatible. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3865976/104967112-2f6d4480-59a8-11eb-82c4-9588f2b01461.png)

Reminder, I can still connect to this server with no issues.

In full disclosure, I haven't narrowed this down to *exclusively* this mod being one cause of it, however I have looked up the [debug.log](https://gist.github.com/Moleculor/cf11121debbcba6fd89fba58a22053e9) which shows 

```
[18Jan2021 15:53:28.651] [Netty Client IO #2/DEBUG] [net.minecraftforge.fml.client.ClientHooks/CLIENTHOOKS]: Received FML ping data from server at moleculor.mcserver.us: FMLNETVER=2, mod list is compatible : false, channel list is compatible: true, extra server mods: {}
[18Jan2021 15:53:28.651] [Netty Client IO #2/INFO] [net.minecraftforge.fml.client.ClientHooks/CLIENTHOOKS]: Client has mods that are missing on server: [mightyarchitect, autofish, betteradvancements, blame]
```

As you can see, this mod appears in the list of mods that are "missing on server". 

According to Forge's [documentation](https://mcforge.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts/sides/), a client side only mod...

> ...should override the DISPLAYTEST extension point to make sure that Forge does not think your mod is required on the server, which would lead to the server being shown as incompatible. For that, put something similar to this into your main mod class constructor: 
```
//Make sure the mod being absent on the other network side does not cause the client to display the server as incompatible
ModLoadingContext.get().registerExtensionPoint(ExtensionPoint.DISPLAYTEST, () -> Pair.of(() -> FMLNetworkConstants.IGNORESERVERONLY, (a, b) -> true));
```

As I do not seem to be able to pull up `DISPLAYTEST` in a search of this repository, I suspect the above (or something equivalent) has not been done. 

I would like to request it, or something like it, be done? Please? 😀

Greetings.
As I was recently trying to texture the assets for this mod, I came along some unpredictabilities regarding the colors this mod uses for its GUI textures. I will list some of my concerns:
1. The 4th sprite in the widgets.png is very confusing. It basically acts as an overlay, but to what degree and what is its function in the first place?
